name: NoPac Scanner - CVE-2021-42278/42287 Check
description: Checks if a domain is vulnerable to the NoPac attack (CVE-2021-42278 + CVE-2021-42287). Prints the domain SID and confirms if the DC is impersonatable. Low noise — just LDAP enumeration. Run this before attempting the exploit to confirm vulnerability and save time.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== NOPAC EXPLAINED (CVE-2021-42278 + CVE-2021-42287) ===
Two separate CVEs chain together:

CVE-2021-42278: Machine account names should end with '$' but nothing enforces this.
Any domain user can create a machine account (default quota: 10) and name it anything,
including 'DC01' — the same name as the actual Domain Controller (without the $).

CVE-2021-42287: When Kerberos can't find the account that was used in the AS-REQ
(e.g. the machine account was renamed AFTER the TGT was issued), it looks for
'<name>$' — and finds the REAL DC. The KDC issues a service ticket AS if the TGT
was issued FOR the real DC account.

Combined: create machine account named 'DC01', get TGT, rename account to something
else, request service ticket — KDC looks for 'DC01$' and finds the REAL DC, issuing
you a ticket with DA-level privileges. One step from DA with any domain creds.

=== WHAT THE SCANNER RETURNS ===
  ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota = 10  → can create machine accounts, VULNERABLE
  ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota = 0   → cannot create machine accounts, NOT vulnerable
  Domain SID: S-1-5-21-...        → needed for the exploit

=== REQUIREMENTS ===
  - Any valid domain credentials
  - ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota > 0 (default is 10 in most environments)
  - Domain controllers running unpatched Windows (pre-November 2021 patches)
  - scanner.py from: github.com/Ridter/noPac

references.title: HTB Academy - Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks

recommended.note: Run the exploit to impersonate Administrator.

defense.why_it_works: NoPac chains CVE-2021-42278 (a domain user renames a machine account's sAMAccountName to match a DC's, minus the trailing $) with CVE-2021-42287 (KDC ticket confusion) to obtain a Kerberos TGT impersonating the Domain Controller - a path from ANY domain user to Domain Admin. This card checks whether a DC is vulnerable.
defense.prerequisites: Any valid domain user account and network access to a Domain Controller. The full exploit also needs ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota > 0 so a non-admin can create a machine account.
defense.impact: Confirmation that the DC is unpatched and vulnerable to NoPac - i.e. a domain-user-to-Domain-Admin escalation is available.
defense.detection: The scan/exploit produces machine-account creation and sAMAccountName changes: Event 4741 (computer account created), 4781/4742 (account name/attribute changed), and anomalous 4768/4769 (TGT/TGS for a DC-named account). A sAMAccountName suddenly matching a DC's name is a high-fidelity indicator.
defense.artifacts: A new machine account (from the account quota); a sAMAccountName modified to a DC name and often reverted; anomalous Kerberos tickets; tool execution (noPac.py / Rubeus) on the attacker host.
defense.prevention: Apply Microsoft's November 2021 updates (KB5008380 / KB5008602), which add PAC validation; set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 so non-admins cannot create machine accounts; alert on sAMAccountName changes and on machine-account creation by non-privileged users.
defense.evasion: Renaming the machine account back after obtaining the ticket hides the sAMAccountName change; using an already-controlled machine account avoids the account-creation event.
defense.misconfiguration: Two AD design flaws combined: (1) CVE-2021-42278 — non-admin domain users can rename computer accounts to impersonate DCs (the sAMAccountName attribute on a computer object they own can be set to any value); (2) CVE-2021-42287 — the KDC's PAC validation falls back to a user-account lookup when a machine-account ticket is requested, allowing privilege escalation. Together, a low-priv user creates a computer (ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota default = 10), renames it to the DC name, requests a TGT, renames it back, then obtains a ticket with Domain Admin rights.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Default insecure settings that enable NoPac:
# 1. ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota >= 1 (default = 10)
Get-ADObject (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName -Properties ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota
# ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota: 10  <-- any user can add 10 computers

# 2. November 2021 patches NOT applied:
# KB5008102 (CVE-2021-42278) + KB5008380 (CVE-2021-42287)
Get-HotFix -Id KB5008102  # empty output = unpatched
defense.secure_config:
# Fix 1 — Set MachineAccountQuota to 0 (block non-admin machine joins):
Set-ADDomain -Identity corp.local -Replace @{'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'=0}

# Fix 2 — Apply patches:
# KB5008102 (Oct 2021 cumulative) + KB5008380 (Nov 2021 cumulative)
# Verify: Get-HotFix -Id KB5008102, KB5008380

# Fix 3 — Enforce PAC validation (registry, post-patch):
# HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Kdc
#   PacRequestorEnforcement = 2  (fully enforce after 2023-04-11 deadline)

# Detection: 4741 (computer account created) + 4781 (renamed) in rapid succession
